question: What are the indications for alteplase?

supports.quote: Intravenous alteplase (recombinant tissue plasminogen activator) is the only approved thrombolytic agent at present indicated for acute ischaemic stoke.
Alteplase has been used successfully in evolving myocardial infarction (MI) to reopen occluded coronary arteries.
However, alteplase is useful in treating pulmonary thromboembolism and peripheral vascular disease.

The trials used to support Food and Drug Administration approval of alteplase for central venous catheter (CVC) occlusions generally had low pediatric enrollment; however, additional small studies are available that support use of alteplase for this indication in children.
Alteplase appears to show efficacy for treatment of thrombus-related venous catheter occlusion in pediatric patients; however, data regarding its use in occluded dialysis catheters are limited.

The efficacy of intravenous alteplase in the treatment of pulmonary thromboembolism has also been established and appears to be similar to that of streptokinase and urokinase in this indication and in arterial thrombotic occlusion.

Further, preliminary data suggest efficacy in the therapy of deep vein thrombosis and arterial thrombotic occlusion, and alteplase has a proven place in the fibrinolytic treatment of pulmonary thromboembolism.

initial_executor.limitations: Evidence indicates approval for acute ischaemic stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary thromboembolism, and central venous catheter occlusions. Use in deep vein thrombosis and arterial thrombotic occlusion is supported by preliminary data or efficacy studies but not necessarily formal approval in all contexts. Data for dialysis catheters is limited. Some indications are restricted by time windows (e.g., within 3 hours for stroke) or specific patient selection criteria.
